case_name: Basavaraja & Ors. v State Of Karnataka
respondent:
State Of Karnataka
Supreme Court of India

22 September 2008
Criminal Appeal No.1 Of 2002
The Judgment was delivered by : Dr. Arijit Pasayat J.
1.  Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court setting aside the acquittal of the appellant as was recorded by learned Sessions Judge, Chitradurga in SC No.82 of 1994. The trial court had acquitted the appellants for charge of commission of offence punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC').
The prosecution case in a nutshell is as follows:
2. On 30.4.1994 at about 1 p.m. the appellant herein had assaulted one Smt. Umadevi (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased') with an intention to cause her death, dragged her inside the cattle shed, where the accused No.2 poured kerosene oil on her person and accused No.1 set fire to her after lighting a match stick as a result of which, the said Smt. Umadevi sustained burn injuries and died. The
facts: On 30.4.1994 at about 1 p.m., the appellant had assaulted one Smt. Umadevi with an intention to cause her death, dragged her inside the cattle shed, where the accused No.2 poured kerosene oil on her person and accused No.1 set fire to her after lighting a match stick as a result of which, the said Smt. Umadevi sustained burn injuries and died.
The deceased Smt. Umadevi had been married to the accused No.1. The accused No.3 Sarmangalamma had been married to the complainant-PW 1 Virupakshappa.

All these accused persons were residing together in the same house. The deceased Umadevi had been telling to PW-3 Jayamma, the wife of PW.2, whenever she used to go to the house of Umadevi, that she was being ill-treated and assaulted by the accused on the ground that she was ugly to look at and was also of unsound mind.
The occurrence took place at 11 AM on 30.4.1994 and the FIR was lodged at 11.45 PM as spoken by PWs. 2 & 3.
Thereafter, both PWs. 2 & 3 returned back to their village at about 10 p.m. and informed the said occurrence to all their relatives.
The dead body of the deceased Umadevi was lying in the cattle shed. It was completely charred.

The trial court found that the evidence of the Doctor PW 7 belied the version of PWs. 2 & 3. There was considerable delay in lodging the FIR and the evidence of PWs. 2 & 3 was not reliable and cogent.
issues: What is the cause of death?
Were the accused persons involved in the murder of Smt. Umadevi?
petitioner_arguments: The evidence of PW 7 indicated that the death was due to asphyxia as a result of smothering, not burning.
There was no serious contradiction between the evidence of PWs. 2 & 3 on one hand and PW 7 on the other.
The charge as framed indicated that the cause of death was due to burning after pouring kerosene, but the evidence of PW 7 indicated that the death was due to asphyxia as a result of smothering.
There was no unexplained delay in lodging the FIR.
The occurrence took place at 11 AM on 30.4.1994 and the FIR was lodged at 11.45 PM as spoken by PWs. 2 & 3.
respondent_arguments: The ocular evidence has to get primacy over medical evidence.
Mere hypothetical opinion given by PW 7 cannot be a ground to doubt the veracity of the evidence of PWs. 2 & 3.
There was no delay in lodging the FIR.
The charges framed against the appellant read as follows: 'That you accused Nos. 1 to 5...'
In the examination u/s. 313 of the Code, with reference to the evidence of PW 7 it was stated that the death was due to smothering.'
court_reasoning: The inevitable result is that the appeal has to succeed, the conviction as recorded by the High Court is set aside.
The charges were framed on totally unfounded premises and even in the examination u/s. 313 of the Code, with reference to the evidence of PW 7 it was stated that the death was due to smothering.
If that to be so, the question of the accused persons having caused the death by burning does not arise.
Such casual framing of charge and examination u/s. 313 of the Code is a disturbing feature.
holding: The appeal has to succeed, the conviction as recorded by the High Court is set aside.
The bail bonds of the accused persons for grant of bail in terms of order dated 22.4.2002 stands discharged.
